title: The Weathercock
summary: Perched atop the church steeple, the gilded weathercock spun around with every gust of wind. "I am the guide of the town!" he boasted. "The sun shines for me, and the clouds follow...
full_text:
Perched atop the church steeple, the gilded weathercock spun around with every gust of wind. "I am the guide of the town!" he boasted. "The sun shines for me, and the clouds follow my pointer!"

When the wind died and he stood motionless, he sneered: "The world is boring and stagnant!" When the gale blew from the north, he pointed north; when it veered south, he swung south, constantly changing his convictions.

An old iron cross stood beside him, firm and unmoving through centuries of storms. The weathercock mocked the cross: "You are rigid and out of fashion!"

A violent hurricane snapped the weathercock from his spindle, tumbling him into the street where his hollow tin body was trampled flat, while the steadfast cross remained standing tall against the sky.
moral: Turning with every breeze of opinion leaves one unstable, hollow, and blind to true direction.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Weathercock"?
options: Andersen's tales teach compassion, resilience, and Christian hope
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof

options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
